issues.legal_issue: A plea of res judicata may be decided as a preliminary issue when its resolution requires no determination of disputed facts or mixed questions of law and fact.
material_facts: The suit was dismissed on the preliminary issue of res judicata by reference to the pleadings and judgments in three earlier suits.
The documentary material necessary to decide the plea was before the courts, and the parties had fully argued the issue.
issues.conclusion: Res judicata is not categorically incapable of determination as a preliminary issue; it may be decided preliminarily when no disputed factual or mixed question needs to be resolved.
issues.legal_principle: Order 14 Rule 2 CPC permits preliminary determination of a bar to the suit created by law. Whether res judicata presents a question of law, fact, or both depends on the issue said to have been decided earlier. The plea must be clearly established and the party opposing it must have an opportunity to meet it, as explained in Alka Gupta v. Narender Kumar Gupta. Sushil Kumar Mehta v. Gobind Ram Bohra and Mathura Prasad Bajoo Jaiswal v. Dossibai N.B. Jeejeebhoy explain that the application of res judicata depends on the earlier issue and the relevant facts and law; Madhukar D. Shende and Ram Harakh likewise recognize that the plea may involve mixed questions.

rule.if: civil_suit_with_res_judicata_plea and prior_suit_records_are_before_the_court and parties_have_addressed_the_plea and no_disputed_fact_or_mixed_question_needs_resolution

predicates.civil_suit_with_res_judicata_plea: A party in a civil suit raised res judicata as a bar to the suit.
predicates.prior_suit_records_are_before_the_court: The pleadings and decisions from the earlier proceedings needed to assess the plea were before the court.
predicates.parties_have_addressed_the_plea: The parties had an opportunity to present their arguments on whether the earlier proceedings barred the suit.
predicates.no_disputed_fact_or_mixed_question_needs: Resolving the plea required no determination of a disputed fact or mixed question of law and fact.

issues.definition: When a civil suit raises res judicata, the earlier records are available, the parties have addressed the plea, and no disputed factual or mixed issue needs resolution, the issue may be decided preliminarily.

issues.legal_issue: An earlier representative suit for administration of a trust does not bar a later suit concerning title when the earlier decision did not conclusively determine the title now in issue.
material_facts: The earlier suit was brought representatively by persons interested in a mosque and sought a scheme for its administration and management of its properties.

The property in dispute was considered in the earlier suit, but the court described the predecessor’s right as prima facie and left open steps concerning whether the terms of the grant had been fulfilled.
The earlier suit did not determine whether the predecessor had absolute title or decide the terms or character of the grant.
The later suit sought a declaration concerning the property and possession, and the property had been notified as wakf property after the earlier decision.
issues.conclusion: The earlier representative suit did not bar the later suit because it did not conclusively decide the predecessor’s absolute title, and the matters in issue were distinct.
issues.legal_principle: Section 11 CPC, including Explanation VI, makes a decree in a bona fide representative suit binding on persons interested in the common right; Explanation VIII addresses issues decided by courts of limited jurisdiction. A court considering a scheme under Section 92 CPC may decide a contested title issue when necessary to determine whether the property belongs to the trust, but a finding that is merely incidental or not necessary and essential to the judgment does not ordinarily operate as res judicata. Mahant Pragdasji Guru Bhagwandasji v. Patel Ishwarlalbhai Narsibhai addresses the scope of Section 92 suits; Raje Anandrao v. Shamrao, Ahmad Adam Sait v. M.E. Makhri, R. Venugopala Naidu v. Venkatarayulu Naidu Charities, and Shiromani Gurdwara Parbhandhak Committee v. Mahant Harnam Singh address the binding effect of representative suits. Sajjadanashin Syed M.D.B.E. Edr. v. Musa Dadabhai Ummer states the necessity and essentiality tests; Gram Panchayat of Village Naulakha v. Ujagar Singh and Nand Ram v. Jagdish Prasad address findings that are collateral or not conclusively decided.

rule.if: civil_suit_following_a_representative_trust_suit and prior_suit_sought_trust_administration and later_suit_seeks_title_or_possession and prior_decision_was_only_prima_facie and prior_decision_did_not_determine_absolute_title and property_status_changed_after_prior_decision

predicates.civil_suit_following_a_representative_tr: A civil suit was brought after an earlier representative proceeding concerning the administration of a trust.
predicates.prior_suit_sought_trust_administration: The earlier proceeding sought a scheme for administering a trust and its property.
predicates.later_suit_seeks_title_or_possession: The later proceeding seeks a determination of title, possession, or both concerning the property.
predicates.prior_decision_was_only_prima_facie: The earlier court described the interested person’s right to the property as prima facie rather than conclusive.
predicates.prior_decision_did_not_determine_absolut: The earlier judgment did not decide that the interested person held absolute title to the property.
predicates.property_status_changed_after_prior_deci: The property was given a changed legal or recorded status after the earlier judgment.

issues.definition: A later title or possession suit is not barred by an earlier representative administration suit when the earlier court made only a prima facie finding, did not determine absolute title, and the property’s status changed afterward.

issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree concerning possession and a lease does not bar a later suit on title when the parties did not compromise the title issue.
material_facts: An earlier suit sought a declaration that the property was wakf property and sought possession.
The parties compromised the earlier suit on the lessee’s continued occupation, rent, and eventual surrender of possession.
Neither the compromise nor the decree determined or compromised title to the property.
issues.conclusion: The compromise decree did not bar the later suit on title by res judicata or estoppel by conduct; the provision barring a suit to challenge an unlawful compromise decree did not apply.
issues.legal_principle: A consent or compromise decree is not, strictly, a decision that has been heard and finally decided for Section 11 CPC, but it may create an estoppel by conduct according to its terms. Pulavarthi Venkata Subba Rao v. Valluri Jagannadha Rao and Sunderabai v. Devaji Shankar Deshpande support that distinction. Order 23 Rule 3A CPC bars a suit challenging a compromise decree on the ground that the compromise was unlawful; it does not bar a later suit that raises an issue the compromise did not resolve.

rule.if: civil_suit_after_compromise_decree and prior_decree_was_based_on_compromise and compromise_resolved_only_possession_or_lease and later_suit_raises_title

predicates.civil_suit_after_compromise_decree: A civil suit concerning property was brought after an earlier suit ended in a compromise decree.
predicates.prior_decree_was_based_on_compromise: The earlier decree recorded the parties’ compromise rather than an adjudication after contest.
predicates.compromise_resolved_only_possession_or_l: The compromise addressed possession or leasing arrangements but did not resolve ownership or title.
predicates.later_suit_raises_title: The later suit asks the court to determine title to the property.

issues.definition: A later suit raising title is not barred when the earlier compromise decree resolved possession or lease arrangements but left title unresolved.

issues.legal_issue: A withdrawn suit seeking only an injunction does not bar a later comprehensive suit on title and possession when the earlier suit involved no adjudication on title.
material_facts: An earlier suit sought only to prevent interference with possession and was later withdrawn.
The earlier suit included no adjudication of title.
The later suit seeking substantive relief concerning title and possession had been filed before the earlier suit was withdrawn.
issues.conclusion: The earlier injunction suit did not bar the later suit.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 11 CPC, a matter must have been heard and finally decided to operate as res judicata. A bare injunction suit in which title was neither raised nor adjudicated does not ordinarily bar a later suit in which title is directly in issue. Gram Panchayat of Village Naulakha v. Ujagar Singh and Sajjadanashin Syed M.D.B.E. Edr. v. Musa Dadabhai Ummer support the distinction between an incidental or absent title determination and a conclusive one.

rule.if: civil_suit_after_withdrawn_injunction_suit and earlier_suit_sought_only_injunction and no_title_issue_was_adjudicated and later_suit_seeks_substantive_title_or_possession_relief and later_suit_filed_before_withdrawal

predicates.civil_suit_after_withdrawn_injunction_su: A civil suit was pursued after an earlier suit for an injunction was withdrawn.
predicates.earlier_suit_sought_only_injunction: The earlier suit requested only an order restraining interference with possession.
predicates.no_title_issue_was_adjudicated: The earlier proceeding did not decide the parties’ rights of title to the property.
predicates.later_suit_seeks_substantive_title_or_po: The later suit seeks substantive relief concerning title, possession, or both.
predicates.later_suit_filed_before_withdrawal: The later suit was filed before the earlier injunction suit was withdrawn.

issues.definition: A later substantive suit on title or possession is not barred when the earlier injunction suit made no title determination and the later suit was filed before the earlier suit was withdrawn.
